name: Steve Ballmer
title: The Hired Hand Richer Than His Boss
subtitle: A Ford manager's son from Detroit sells brownie mix, quits Stanford for Bill Gates, runs Microsoft for 14 years, buys an NBA team, and is then suspended from it for a year.
hook: In ==1980==, two students in the same Stanford business school class dropped out. One went home to India to help with his father's business: Mukesh Ambani. The other took a ==$50,000== job, plus a cut of profit growth, at a tiny software firm run by his college friend. __Today that hired hand is worth about $160 billion, some $40 billion more than Bill Gates, the founder who hired him.__ Gates has pledged to give nearly all his wealth away. Ballmer has held on to most of his Microsoft shares.

glance.label: Born
glance.value: March 24, 1956, in Detroit, Michigan, USA, as Steven Anthony Ballmer.

glance.label: Grew up
glance.value: In the Detroit suburbs. His Swiss-born father, Fred, was a manager at Ford. His mother, Bea, was born in Detroit.

glance.label: Education
glance.value: Scholarship to Detroit Country Day School. Harvard, 1977, maths and economics, where he became friends with Bill Gates. Left Stanford's MBA programme after one year.

glance.label: First job
glance.value: Assistant product manager at Procter & Gamble, selling Duncan Hines brownie mix and sharing a cubicle with Jeff Immelt, the future CEO of General Electric.

glance.label: Big break (age 24)
glance.value: Joined Microsoft in June 1980 as its first business manager, on $50,000 a year, plus 10% of the profit growth he generated. He later swapped that for a stake of about 8%. He was a hire, not a founder.

glance.label: Ran Microsoft
glance.value: CEO from 2000 to 2014, after 20 years in other roles there. Revenue was almost $80 billion when he retired.

glance.label: Source of wealth
glance.value: Microsoft shares. Forbes put him at about $160 billion, No. 9 in the world, on 2 November 2026. He says he is still the largest individual investor, and his stake was set to pay close to $1 billion in dividends in fiscal 2024.

glance.label: Today
glance.value: Owner of the LA Clippers, bought for $2 billion in 2014. In September 2026 the NBA suspended him from all league and team activities for one year over salary cap violations. He accepted the penalty, saying disagreements over the findings remain. John S. Gibson runs the team as interim CEO and governor.

glance.label: Giving and civic work
glance.value: Co-founded Ballmer Group with his wife, Connie, and founded USAFacts, a nonpartisan government data project, in 2017. Forbes reports the couple have given away more than $7.4 billion.

glance.label: Family and home
glance.value: Married Connie Snyder in 1990. They have three sons. Lives in the Seattle area of Washington state, USA.

contact.howToReach: We found no public personal email or office line for Steve Ballmer, so the closest routes to his world are USAFacts, the data project he founded (info@usafacts.org), and his X account. Don't pitch him through the Clippers, because he is serving a one-year NBA suspension from all team activities, and the team's published lines handle tickets and fan service. Don't ask Ballmer Group for money either: it says it cannot accept unsolicited grant applications, and it warns that scammers impersonate its founders, so treat anyone offering you Ballmer money or asking you for fees or ID as a fraud. Microsoft's lines reach its investor relations and press teams, not him, since he left in 2014. If you write to USAFacts, keep it under five lines and make it specific, such as one number you checked or one error you found with a link, and count a reply from the team as a win.

factCheck.method: Built on 3 November 2026. Identity and career basics come from Ballmer's own transcripts published by Microsoft, the Clippers' official biography, CNN's research desk, Forbes, Fortune and GeekWire. Wikipedia was used only as a lead. The suspension rests on the NBA's own release and AP. Contact channels were read on each organisation's own page; Microsoft's phone and address come from its FY2026 10-K, read in the copy hosted on Microsoft's investor site because sec.gov refused automated reading. Social handles for organisations were read from links on their own websites, not from the profiles, since X and most LinkedIn pages could not be opened by automated tools. Ballmer's personal X handle therefore rests on Fortune's 2015 report and was not checked live; we could not confirm how active it is today. Left out on purpose: named staff work emails on official pages, numbers from directories and contact-finder sites, and a LinkedIn page under his name that we could not tie to him. Photo licences and authors were read through the Commons API.

disputed.note: Forbes and Fortune say No. 30, and Stanford's write-up calls it a 30-person firm. The host's introduction in Microsoft's own 2003 transcript says No. 24. The glance avoids the number; if used, say 'about the 30th'.

Fortune says he traded his profit deal for 8%. Paul Allen's 2011 memoir says the founders agreed on at most 5%, that Gates offered 8.75%, and that Gates covered the extra from his own shares. Gates said his memory of events may differ from Allen's. We say 'about 8%'.

Fortune says he received no shares at first, only salary and profit share. The 2003 Microsoft transcript introduction says 'some percentage of ownership'. Both fit if the stake came when Microsoft became a corporation, as Fortune describes, so we describe the profit deal first.

disputed.claim: How many Microsoft shares he owns now.
disputed.note: The last disclosed figure is 333.2 million, from 2014. Ballmer told GeekWire in 2025 that he holds fewer than when he left but is still the largest investor. Any current number is an estimate, so we give none.

Forbes' real-time figure read $159.6 billion and $161.7 billion on two reads marked 2 November 2026, against $120.4 billion for Gates, so we say 'about $160 billion'. Bloomberg's index uses different assumptions: $172 billion against $124 billion in July 2025.
Forbes says Hunts Point, Washington. The Clippers' official biography, dated 2017, says Bellevue, Washington. Both are in the Seattle area, which is what we state.

The NBA says he knowingly sought to help Kawhi Leonard obtain off-court income and approved a deal he knew was a precondition for an Aspiration endorsement. His lawyer first called the probe a 'witch hunt'; he later accepted the penalty and apologised, while saying disagreements over the findings remain. ESPN noted the summary report cites no specific evidence that appears to implicate him directly. The New York Times reported a Justice Department inquiry, with sources saying it was uncertain whether charges would follow. We found no report of charges as of 3 November 2026, so treat this as unresolved.
The 2003 Microsoft transcript introduction says a perfect 800, and Ballmer called that background 'pretty close'. Wikipedia says 790. Not used in this file; the early-life writer should check it.
Fortune's 2015 piece gives @clippersteveb, while its 2017 piece gives @clippersteve. We list only @Steven_Ballmer, the handle Fortune reported as confirmed and verified.
Its 2026 annual report gives PO Box 805, Bellevue, WA 98009. Its terms page, last updated in 2018, gives P.O. Box 1558, Bellevue. We list the newer one.
